profile.headline: Aircraft Software Developer
profile.summary:
I support several software programs at Boeing. My Ph.D. research focused on cooperative control systems for autonomous vehicles to optimize network communication.

I am an enthusiastic cycling instructor, and serve on the board of several organizations to grow the cycling population and infrastructure in Oklahoma City. My wife and I are also avid rock climbers and triathletes.

Specialties: Algorithm Design and Optimization, Simulation, Communication Networks and Routing, GUI design, C/C++, MATLAB, DO-178C, MIL-HDBK-516C, NIST 800.53, System Administration, Java, PHP, MySQL, Corporate Community Outreach

positions.title: RECUV Research Assistant
positions.description:
I supported a mixture of projects at the Research and Engineering Center of Unmanned Vehicles - government/policy, defense, and civil. Many involve developing systems for autonomous aircraft to achieve a specific communications objectives among a network of both stationary and mobile nodes.
Some specific projects include:
 -performing survey of unmanned aircraft (UA) performance and technologies to aid in integrating UA into the National Airspace System
 -integrating various customer payloads into unmanned aircraft and supporting their flight experiments
 -using UA to perform weather sensing in tornadic storms
 -developing a combination of motion/communication protocols for UA to enable communication in sparse networks.

My thesis work is on Data Ferrying - taking advantage of an aircraft's mobility to enable (delayed) communication between sensors that otherwise could not communicate with each other. Specifically, I'm optimizing the aircraft's trajectory between sensors to maximize the achievable quality of service. Additionally, I am analyzing the dependence of the vehicle's dynamics and the communication environment on the trajectories to develop efficient heuristics to enable quick on-line trajectory generation for dynamic environments.

positions.title: webmaster
positions.description: I designed the website for the University of Colorado-Boulder cycling team. In addition to site administration, my role involved graphic design and editing, sports journalism, sponsor management, social media management, and more. The website serves as a portal to keep alumni, team members, and the interested community at large up to date with what our cycling team is up to. This includes pictures, race promotion and stories of how our team is performing. Additionally, forums allow team members and coaches to interact with each other, sharing information such as great routes to ride, race tactics, and bike maintenance.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
I was a teaching assistant for the sophomore level aerospace course, Aerospace Vehicle Design and Performance. The class emphasized uncertainty and sensitivity analysis in the context of general aircraft and spacecraft dynamics. The heavy lab component that complimented the lecture portion involved wind tunnel testing and analysis of an F-16, as well as testing, modeling and designing a bottle rocket.

With a course of 97 students, it was necessary to have 2 TAs and 2 additional course assistants. I developed exam-style questions and led recitations throughout the semester, I guided students in the lab along with another TA, and did a portion of grading.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Through several school breaks between 2005 and 2007, I assisted in the upgrading and redesign of the company's primary data-mining software, as well as the customer interface and website. This included database design and optimization, query optimization, user-load-balancing, information security measures, and of course, thorough testing and documentation.

positions.title: Opto-mechanical engineer
positions.description: As my co-op while at IIT, I aided in the development and testing of specific defense equipment. I heavily used Pro-Engineer to design components to be manufactured. I also researched the effects of high-speed rain drop impacts on our equipment, culminating in designing an experiment that simulates the environment for less than 5% of the cost of a full-scale test. My experiment identified a seal problem quickly and cheaply.

volunteerExperiences.description:
With the CU Cycling Team, I helped manage more than 100 student athletes compete in several competitive seasons with travel throughout the Rocky Mountains, as well as national championships throughout the country. A major part of this is hosting fund-raising events as well as races for the community.

The biggest of these events is our Summer Short Track Mountain Bike series, hosting a race every Wednesday over the summer. This involves working with Boulder Parks and Recreation and the Boulder community at large, designing race courses, scheduling and coordinating volunteers, advertising and marketing the series, seeking sponsorship and merchandise for race prizes, scoring and posting results, and more. This series raises between $10k-$15k for the team, with another $3k+ raised for the city of Boulder.

For the cycling community, we have a fun kids race for children under 8 years old, and all junior racers (18 and under) race for free to promote their development in the sport. We also promote equality in the sport through equal payouts for Men's and Women's races.
